results.name: trial_index_yes_slope
results.description: OLS slope of rating on trial_index, in change of yes-probability per 100 trials; t_observed above null_mean (~0) means people drift toward saying yes over the session, which the stationary model cannot produce (below = drift toward no).

results.name: ruleless_multi_far_unmatched_yes
results.description: In sets of >=2 examples with no explicit rule (mixed final digits, common factor <3), yes rate for non-example targets sharing no final digit with any example and lying >=2 decades outside the examples' band; t_observed above null_mean means people give rule-less sets a broad "anything goes" acceptance the model lacks; below means the model over-generalizes far from rule-less sets.
results.code:
# name: ruleless_multi_far_unmatched_yes
# description: In sets of >=2 examples with no explicit rule (mixed final digits, common factor <3), yes rate for non-example targets sharing no final digit with any example and lying >=2 decades outside the examples' band; t_observed above null_mean means people give rule-less sets a broad "anything goes" acceptance the model lacks; below means the model over-generalizes far from rule-less sets.
import math
from functools import reduce
def test_statistic(df):
    sets = df["number_set"].astype(str)
    info = {}
    for s in sets.unique():
        xs = [int(v) for v in s.split(",")]
        g = reduce(math.gcd, xs)
        uni = len({x % 10 for x in xs}) == 1
        ruleless = len(xs) >= 2 and not (uni or g >= 3)
        info[s] = (ruleless, min(x // 10 for x in xs), max(x // 10 for x in xs))
    rl = sets.map(lambda s: info[s][0]).to_numpy().astype(bool)
    lo = sets.map(lambda s: info[s][1]).to_numpy().astype(int)
    hi = sets.map(lambda s: info[s][2]).to_numpy().astype(int)
    t = df["target"].astype(int).to_numpy()
    ex = sets.str.split(",", expand=True).apply(pd.to_numeric, errors="coerce").to_numpy()
    in_set = (ex == t[:, None]).any(axis=1)
    digit_match = (np.mod(ex, 10) == (t % 10)[:, None]).any(axis=1)
    td = t // 10
    gap = np.maximum(np.maximum(lo - td, 0), td - hi)
    m = rl & ~in_set & ~digit_match & (gap >= 2)
    if m.sum() == 0:
        return 0.0
    return float(df["rating"].astype(float).to_numpy()[m].mean())

results.name: set_yes_rate_dispersion
results.description: SD across number_sets of the set-level yes rate on targets that are not examples; t_observed above null_mean means generalization breadth still differs more between sets (some near all-no, others near all-yes) than the rule-gated model produces; below means the model over-differentiates sets.
results.code:
# name: set_yes_rate_dispersion
# description: SD across number_sets of the set-level yes rate on targets that are not examples; t_observed above null_mean means generalization breadth still differs more between sets (some near all-no, others near all-yes) than the rule-gated model produces; below means the model over-differentiates sets.
def test_statistic(df):
    ex = df["number_set"].str.split(",", expand=True).apply(pd.to_numeric, errors="coerce").to_numpy()
    t = df["target"].astype(int).to_numpy()
    in_set = (ex == t[:, None]).any(axis=1)
    sub = df.loc[~in_set]
    rates = sub.groupby("number_set")["rating"].mean()
    if len(rates) < 2:
        return 0.0
    return float(rates.std())

results.name: rule_set_in_band_nonrule_yes
results.description: In sets of >=2 examples with an explicit rule (shared final digit or common factor >=3), yes rate for non-example targets that violate the rule, share no final digit with any example, but lie within the examples' decade band; t_observed above null_mean means magnitude familiarity survives rule detection more than the model's magnitude_preempt allows; below means rules suppress "nearby" more.
results.code:
# name: rule_set_in_band_nonrule_yes
# description: In sets of >=2 examples with an explicit rule (shared final digit or common factor >=3), yes rate for non-example targets that violate the rule, share no final digit with any example, but lie within the examples' decade band; t_observed above null_mean means magnitude familiarity survives rule detection more than the model's magnitude_preempt allows; below means rules suppress "nearby" more.
import math
from functools import reduce
def test_statistic(df):
    sets = df["number_set"].astype(str)
    info = {}
    for s in sets.unique():
        xs = [int(v) for v in s.split(",")]
        g = reduce(math.gcd, xs)
        uni = len({x % 10 for x in xs}) == 1
        rule = len(xs) >= 2 and (uni or g >= 3)
        info[s] = (rule, g if g >= 3 else 0, min(x // 10 for x in xs), max(x // 10 for x in xs))
    rule = sets.map(lambda s: info[s][0]).to_numpy().astype(bool)
    g = sets.map(lambda s: info[s][1]).to_numpy().astype(int)
    lo = sets.map(lambda s: info[s][2]).to_numpy().astype(int)
    hi = sets.map(lambda s: info[s][3]).to_numpy().astype(int)
    t = df["target"].astype(int).to_numpy()
    ex = sets.str.split(",", expand=True).apply(pd.to_numeric, errors="coerce").to_numpy()
    in_set = (ex == t[:, None]).any(axis=1)
    digit_match = (np.mod(ex, 10) == (t % 10)[:, None]).any(axis=1)
    mult = (g > 0) & (t % np.where(g > 0, g, 1) == 0)
    td = t // 10
    in_band = (td >= lo) & (td <= hi)
    m = rule & ~in_set & ~digit_match & ~mult & in_band
    if m.sum() == 0:
        return 0.0
    return float(df["rating"].astype(float).to_numpy()[m].mean())

results.name: rule_set_obey_minus_violate_gap
results.description: In sets of >=2 examples with an explicit rule (all share a final digit, or common factor g>=3), yes rate for non-example targets obeying the rule (same final digit / multiple of g) minus targets violating it; t_observed above null_mean means people apply detected rules more sharply (all-or-none) than the model's graded features; below means the model over-sharpens rules.

results.name: partial_digit_match_mixed_set_yes
results.description: In sets of >=3 examples with >=2 distinct final digits, yes rate for non-example targets whose final digit matches exactly one example; t_observed above null_mean means a single digit match counts as a full match (max-like), not the 1/n share the model's averaged similarity gives; below means partial matches count even less than averaged.
results.code:
# name: partial_digit_match_mixed_set_yes
# description: In sets of >=3 examples with >=2 distinct final digits, yes rate for non-example targets whose final digit matches exactly one example; t_observed above null_mean means a single digit match counts as a full match (max-like), not the 1/n share the model's averaged similarity gives; below means partial matches count even less than averaged.
def test_statistic(df):
    ex = df["number_set"].str.split(",", expand=True).apply(pd.to_numeric, errors="coerce").to_numpy()
    n = np.isfinite(ex).sum(axis=1)
    d = np.mod(ex, 10)
    nd = pd.DataFrame(d).nunique(axis=1).to_numpy()
    t = df["target"].astype(int).to_numpy()
    in_set = (ex == t[:, None]).any(axis=1)
    k = (d == (t % 10)[:, None]).sum(axis=1)
    m = (n >= 3) & (nd >= 2) & (~in_set) & (k == 1)
    if m.sum() == 0:
        return 0.0
    return float(df["rating"].astype(float).to_numpy()[m].mean())

results.name: round_target_even_unmatched_gap
results.description: Among even, non-example targets sharing no final digit with any example (so no example ends in 0), yes rate for round targets (multiples of 10) minus other even targets; t_observed above null_mean means people favour round numbers as program outputs beyond the model's parity credit; below means round numbers are disfavoured.
results.code:
# name: round_target_even_unmatched_gap
# description: Among even, non-example targets sharing no final digit with any example (so no example ends in 0), yes rate for round targets (multiples of 10) minus other even targets; t_observed above null_mean means people favour round numbers as program outputs beyond the model's parity credit; below means round numbers are disfavoured.
def test_statistic(df):
    ex = df["number_set"].str.split(",", expand=True).apply(pd.to_numeric, errors="coerce").to_numpy()
    t = df["target"].astype(int).to_numpy()
    in_set = (ex == t[:, None]).any(axis=1)
    digit_match = (np.mod(ex, 10) == (t % 10)[:, None]).any(axis=1)
    base = (~in_set) & (~digit_match) & (t % 2 == 0)
    y = df["rating"].astype(float).to_numpy()
    rnd = base & (t % 10 == 0)
    oth = base & (t % 10 != 0)
    if rnd.sum() == 0 or oth.sum() == 0:
        return 0.0
    return float(y[rnd].mean() - y[oth].mean())

results.name: single_example_magnitude_slope
results.description: Among single-example sets (targets other than the example), OLS slope of rating on log10(example value); t_observed below null_mean means people generalize more broadly from small examples (e.g. 5, 8) than from large ones (e.g. 91, 100) beyond what digit/band features predict; above means the reverse.
results.code:
# name: single_example_magnitude_slope
# description: Among single-example sets (targets other than the example), OLS slope of rating on log10(example value); t_observed below null_mean means people generalize more broadly from small examples (e.g. 5, 8) than from large ones (e.g. 91, 100) beyond what digit/band features predict; above means the reverse.
def test_statistic(df):
    ns = df["number_set"].astype(str)
    single = ~ns.str.contains(",")
    sub = df.loc[single]
    x = pd.to_numeric(sub["number_set"], errors="coerce").to_numpy().astype(float)
    t = sub["target"].astype(int).to_numpy()
    keep = (x != t) & np.isfinite(x)
    if keep.sum() < 3:
        return 0.0
    lx = np.log10(x[keep])
    y = sub["rating"].astype(float).to_numpy()[keep]
    xc = lx - lx.mean()
    den = float((xc ** 2).sum())
    if den <= 0:
        return 0.0
    return float((xc * (y - y.mean())).sum() / den)
